```tsx presets/stories/demo.tsx
'use client';

import { Lightbox, type LightboxItem } from './lightbox';

/**
 * App-level demo — not part of the copy-paste package.
 *
 * A horizontally scrolling story tray. Each circle is a `Lightbox.Trigger`
 * showing the author’s portrait. `crossfade="both"`: the face is not the
 * 9:16 frame, so a geometry morph would look wrong. Closing from a story
 * whose trigger has scrolled off-screen recenters it for the close.
 */

function mixkit(id: number): string {
  return `https://assets.mixkit.co/videos/${id}/${id}-720.mp4`;
}

/** Mixkit’s first generated 720p still — matches the opening frame of `${id}-720.mp4`. */
function mixkitPoster(id: number): string {
  return `https://assets.mixkit.co/videos/${id}/${id}-thumb-720-0.jpg`;
}

function portrait(gender: 'women' | 'men', n: number): string {
  return `https://randomuser.me/api/portraits/${gender}/${n}.jpg`;
}

const stories: LightboxItem[] = [
  {
    id: 'maya',
    name: 'Maya',
    time: '2h',
    avatar: portrait('women', 44),
    poster: mixkitPoster(40065),
    video: mixkit(40065),
    alt: 'Maya’s story',
    width: 720,
    height: 1280,
  },
  {
    id: 'julian',
    name: 'Julian',
    time: '5h',
    avatar: portrait('men', 32),
    poster: mixkitPoster(43000),
    video: mixkit(43000),
    alt: 'Julian’s story',
    width: 720,
    height: 1280,
  },
  {
    id: 'noor',
    name: 'Noor',
    time: '8h',
    avatar: portrait('women', 68),
    poster: mixkitPoster(43785),
    video: mixkit(43785),
    alt: 'Noor’s story',
    width: 720,
    height: 1280,
  },
  {
    id: 'eli',
    name: 'Eli',
    time: '12h',
    avatar: portrait('men', 75),
    poster: mixkitPoster(40064),
    video: mixkit(40064),
    alt: 'Eli’s story',
    width: 720,
    height: 1280,
  },
  {
    id: 'sam',
    name: 'Sam',
    time: '1d',
    avatar: portrait('men', 22),
    poster: mixkitPoster(44852),
    video: mixkit(44852),
    alt: 'Sam’s story',
    width: 720,
    height: 1280,
  },
  {
    id: 'priya',
    name: 'Priya',
    time: '1d',
    avatar: portrait('women', 21),
    poster: mixkitPoster(50000),
    video: mixkit(50000),
    alt: 'Priya’s story',
    width: 720,
    height: 1280,
  },
  {
    id: 'tomas',
    name: 'Tomás',
    time: '2d',
    avatar: portrait('men', 11),
    poster: mixkitPoster(44600),
    video: mixkit(44600),
    alt: 'Tomás’s story',
    width: 720,
    height: 1280,
  },
  {
    id: 'aisha',
    name: 'Aisha',
    time: '2d',
    avatar: portrait('women', 17),
    poster: mixkitPoster(40066),
    video: mixkit(40066),
    alt: 'Aisha’s story',
    width: 720,
    height: 1280,
  },
];

export function StoriesPresetDemo() {
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xl">
      <Lightbox.Root
        loop
        viewTransition="snappy"
        // Avatar is a different image from the 9:16 frame, so every trigger
        // crossfades — skip the decode wait so the dissolve starts immediately.
        awaitImageDecode={false}
        // Avatar tray is a horizontal scroller: recenter the active circle
        // between snapshot captures so the close dissolve lands on-screen
        // without a painted jump. Avoid `onChange` — scrolling the page
        // under an open viewer can flash tiles on iOS Safari.
        scrollTriggerIntoView={[
          { type: 'onOpenComplete', behavior: 'instant', inline: 'nearest' },
          { type: 'onChange', behavior: 'instant', inline: 'nearest' },
        ]}
      >
        <p className="px-1 text-[13px] font-semibold tracking-tight text-neutral-900 dark:text-neutral-50">
          Stories
        </p>
        <ul className="mt-3 flex snap-x snap-proximity gap-4 overflow-x-auto px-1 pb-1 scrollbar-none">
          {stories.map((story, i) => (
            <li
              key={story.id}
              className="flex w-16 shrink-0 snap-center scroll-mx-4 flex-col items-center gap-1.5"
            >
              <Lightbox.Trigger index={i} aria-label={`${story.name}’s story`} crossfade="both">
                {({ imageRef }) => (
                  <img
                    ref={imageRef}
                    src={story.avatar}
                    alt=""
                    width={56}
                    height={56}
                    className="block size-14 rounded-full object-cover"
                    draggable={false}
                  />
                )}
              </Lightbox.Trigger>
              <span className="w-full truncate text-center text-[11px] leading-tight text-neutral-600 dark:text-neutral-400">
                {story.name}
              </span>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>

        <Lightbox.Gallery items={stories} ariaLabel="Stories" />
      </Lightbox.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

# Photos app

# Photos app (RTL)

The same photos app mirrored for a right-to-left locale — dir="rtl" on Lightbox.Root mirrors navigation, the thumbnail strip, and the arrow keys.

## Source

```tsx examples/lightbox/photos-app-rtl/page.tsx
import type { Metadata } from 'next';

import { PhotosAppView } from '../photos-app/photos-app-view';

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: 'Photos app example (RTL)',
  description:
    'The photos app example mirrored for a right-to-left locale: dir="rtl" on Lightbox.Root mirrors navigation, the thumbnail strip, and the arrow keys.',
};

/**
 * The photos app mirrored for a right-to-left locale.
 *
 * Same composition, two changes: `dir="rtl"` on `Lightbox.Root` (which mirrors
 * navigation, the thumbnail strip, and the arrow keys) and `dir="rtl"` on
 * `<html>` (which mirrors the layout). Both are needed — the prop drives
 * behavior and CSS drives paint, and the library warns in development when they
 * disagree.
 */
export default function PhotosAppRtlPage() {
  return <PhotosAppView dir="rtl" />;
}
```

# Infinite scroll

An endless feed where the lightbox paginates too — one photo array drives grid tiles and slides; the grid loads pages via an IntersectionObserver sentinel, and onValueChange fetches ahead inside the open viewer. The viewer is Lightbox.VirtualSlides: only a window of slides around the active index is mounted, so the native scroll-snap track stays cheap however long the feed grows, with a minimal Previous/Next chrome (no thumbnails).

## Source

```tsx examples/lightbox/infinite-scroll/page.tsx
import type { Metadata } from 'next';

import { InfiniteScrollFeed } from './infinite-scroll-feed';

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: 'Infinite scroll example',
  description:
    'An endless photo feed whose lightbox paginates too: swiping near the end fetches the next page and appends slides to the native scroll-snap track while the viewer stays open, built with ramka.',
};

export default function InfiniteScrollPage() {
  return <InfiniteScrollFeed />;
}
```

# URL-synced state

Masonry wall wired to Next.js dynamic routes ([[...id]]) — every photo is a shareable URL: deep links open the viewer on that slide, swiping rewrites the URL in place, and browser Back closes the viewer.

## Source

```tsx examples/lightbox/url-synced-state/[[...id]]/page.tsx
import type { Metadata } from 'next';
import { notFound } from 'next/navigation';

import { UrlSyncedStateDemo } from '../url-synced-state-demo';
import { GALLERY_PAGE_TITLE, galleryPhotos, photoPageTitle } from '../photos';

/**
 * Optional catch-all: `/examples/lightbox/url-synced-state` renders the grid,
 * and `/examples/lightbox/url-synced-state/5` is the same page deep-linked
 * into the lightbox — the client demo reads the photo id from the pathname and
 * opens on that slide. One route (one page component) for both URL shapes
 * means client-side URL changes reconcile into the same mounted tree, so the
 * viewer never remounts while it rewrites the URL.
 */
interface UrlSyncedStateRouteProps {
  params: Promise<{ id?: string[] }>;
}

/** Prerender the grid plus every photo permalink. */
export function generateStaticParams() {
  return [{ id: [] }, ...galleryPhotos.map((photo) => ({ id: [photo.id] }))];
}

export async function generateMetadata({ params }: UrlSyncedStateRouteProps): Promise<Metadata> {
  const { id } = await params;
  const photo = id?.length ? galleryPhotos.find((p) => p.id === id[0]) : undefined;
  if (photo) {
    const title = photoPageTitle(photo);
    const description = `${photo.alt} — a deep link straight into the lightbox, driven by a Next.js dynamic route and ramka's controlled open/value props.`;
    return {
      title,
      description,
      // `title`/`description` alone don't cascade into the OpenGraph object
      // inherited from the root layout — without an explicit `openGraph` here,
      // a shared photo URL unfurls as the generic site card. This is the
      // "shareable URL with per-photo metadata" half of the demo's pitch, so
      // give crawlers the actual photo. `StaticImageData` supplies a
      // site-relative `src` plus intrinsic dimensions; the root layout's
      // `metadataBase` resolves it to an absolute URL. (Per-photo canonicals
      // come free — the root layout's `canonical: './'` resolves per page.)
      openGraph: {
        title,
        description: photo.alt,
        images: [
          {
            url: photo.image.src,
            width: photo.image.width,
            height: photo.image.height,
            alt: photo.alt,
          },
        ],
      },
      twitter: { card: 'summary_large_image' },
    };
  }
  return {
    title: GALLERY_PAGE_TITLE,
    description:
      'A masonry lightbox wired to Next.js dynamic routes: every photo is a shareable URL — deep links open the viewer, swipes rewrite the URL, browser Back closes it. Built with ramka.',
  };
}

export default async function UrlSyncedStateRoute({ params }: UrlSyncedStateRouteProps) {
  const { id } = await params;
  // Unknown photo ids 404 like any other dynamic route. `id?.length` (not
  // `id &&`): the grid's static param is literally `{ id: [] }`, and an empty
  // array is truthy — Next currently normalizes it to `undefined` at prerender
  // time, but the guard shouldn't lean on that.
  if (id?.length && (id.length > 1 || !galleryPhotos.some((photo) => photo.id === id[0]))) {
    notFound();
  }
  return <UrlSyncedStateDemo />;
}
```

```tsx examples/lightbox/url-synced-state/url-synced-state-demo.tsx
'use client';

import * as React from 'react';
import Image from 'next/image';
import { usePathname } from 'next/navigation';
import * as Lightbox from '@ramka/react/lightbox';

import { ExampleShell } from '../../../../_components/example-shell';
import {
  LightboxGallery,
  triggerFocusClass,
} from '../../../../_components/lightbox-chrome';
import { GALLERY_PAGE_TITLE, galleryPhotos, photoPageTitle } from './photos';

/**
 * The grid renders at this route; every photo also exists as its own URL under
 * the `[[...id]]` optional catch-all — `/examples/lightbox/url-synced-state/5` —
 * so slides are shareable, deep-linkable pages with their own metadata (see
 * `[[...id]]/page.tsx`).
 */
const BASE_PATH = '/examples/lightbox/url-synced-state';

const items = galleryPhotos.map((photo) => ({
  ...photo,
  src: photo.image,
  thumb: photo.image,
}));

/** `/…/url-synced-state/5` → 4; the bare grid URL (or an unknown id) → -1. */
function photoIndexFromPathname(pathname: string): number {
  if (!pathname.startsWith(`${BASE_PATH}/`)) return -1;
  // decodeURIComponent throws on malformed percent-sequences. Navigation can't
  // deliver one (the server 400s those before rendering), but any code calling
  // pushState with an arbitrary string can — treat it as "not a photo URL".
  let id: string;
  try {
    id = decodeURIComponent(pathname.slice(BASE_PATH.length + 1));
  } catch {
    return -1;
  }
  return galleryPhotos.findIndex((photo) => photo.id === id);
}

/**
 * Masonry inputs (see masonry-grid.css for the layout itself and the full
 * design rationale). A column is 120 row-units wide, a gap is 9; a tile's
 * span is its aspect-derived height in those units plus its own bottom gap.
 * Unit-relative means the SAME span works at both breakpoints — the number
 * can live in the server HTML and the column switch is pure CSS, which is
 * what makes the server paint correct at any viewport (a JS column count
 * guessed 2 on the server and visibly re-bucketed desktop visits to 3 after
 * hydration). The photos are exact 2:3 / 3:2 / 1:1 crops, so the spans are
 * exact integers — no rounding crop from the `object-cover` below.
 */
const MASONRY_COL_UNITS = 120;
const MASONRY_GAP_UNITS = 9;

function masonrySpan(image: { width: number; height: number }): number {
  return Math.round((MASONRY_COL_UNITS * image.height) / image.width) + MASONRY_GAP_UNITS;
}

export function UrlSyncedStateDemo() {
  // Single URL source. `usePathname` updates on native History API writes
  // (Next.js shallow routing) AND on browser back/forward, so one hook covers
  // deep links, swipes, and the Back button.
  const pathname = usePathname();
  const urlIndex = photoIndexFromPathname(pathname);

  // Local state is the lightbox's source of truth; the URL mirrors it. Driving
  // `open` straight from the pathname would also work, but a trigger tap would
  // then wait for the routing round-trip before the open lands — and the
  // library only runs the view-transition morph when open flips through its
  // own gesture path (Trigger / Close / Escape / pull-to-dismiss). Controlled
  // props updated synchronously from the callbacks keep that path intact.
  //
  // Deep links hydrate OPEN — the photo page loads with the viewer already in
  // the server HTML, no post-hydration pop-in. That is only possible because
  // deep-link visits skip the body portal (see `deepLinkVisit` below): a
  // portal target like `document.body` does not exist during server rendering,
  // so a server render with `open={true}` plus a real portal is a guaranteed
  // hydration mismatch. In-place rendering is deterministic on both sides.
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(urlIndex !== -1);
  const [index, setIndex] = React.useState(urlIndex === -1 ? 0 : urlIndex);

  // Decided ONCE per mount, never mid-session: swapping `container` would
  // reparent the portal subtree and remount an open viewer. Deep-link visits
  // render the viewer in place (`container: null`) so it exists in the server
  // HTML; regular visits portal to document.body as usual. The in-place host
  // gets `relative z-50` so the fixed viewer stacks above the docs page's
  // sticky mobile header (z-40) — portaled hosts win by document order and
  // must NOT carry a z-index (it would stack above body-level tooltips).
  // Note this branch isn't strictly "the server rendered this": a client-side
  // remount at a photo URL (open a photo, navigate to another docs page, press
  // Back without bfcache) also mounts with `urlIndex !== -1` and takes the
  // in-place path. That's fine — it renders identically — the only difference
  // is the SSR flags below briefly suppress an open fade nobody would see.
  const [deepLinkVisit] = React.useState(urlIndex !== -1);

  // Destination blur is the ONE exception to the Next.js Image guide's rule
  // ("index has a trigger image → no destination blur"). That rule exists
  // because on gesture opens Ramka paints the trigger's already-decoded image
  // behind the destination, and an LQIP would cover that sharp bridge with a
  // blurry one. A deep-link visit has no gesture: the bridge can't paint
  // before hydration and the grid image is cold-loading in parallel — while
  // `blurDataURL` is inlined into the server HTML, making it the only
  // placeholder that can exist on first paint. So: blur destinations for
  // deep-link visits, keep them clean for regular visits. Per-mount like the
  // portal decision above; the (unchanged) LQIP background layers behind
  // already-loaded pixels, so later in-session opens stay bridged and sharp.
  const galleryItems = React.useMemo(
    () => (deepLinkVisit ? items.map((item) => ({ ...item, destinationBlur: true })) : items),
    [deepLinkVisit],
  );

  // Deep links paint the RIGHT photo before hydration via the library's
  // `Slides ssrSlideShift` (passed through LightboxGallery below): the server
  // HTML carries a transform that translates every slide by
  // `-index × slide width` so the deep-linked photo sits at scroll offset 0,
  // and the library swaps the real scroll in — same commit, one paint — at
  // hydration. The skin's only obligation is mirroring the track's gap into
  // `--lightbox-ssr-slide-gap` (see lightbox-chrome.tsx, next to the gap
  // utilities it restates).

  // A server-rendered open viewer must not FADE in — the skin's open fades run
  // off @starting-style, which applies on first render, and for SSR'd markup
  // first render is page load. While this flag is on, a host class flattens
  // every transition inside (ssr-no-transitions.css) so the server paint is
  // the final frame. Removed one frame AFTER the first post-hydration paint —
  // transitions consult the after-change style, so a layout-effect removal
  // (same style recalc where the strip's data-positioned lands) would restart
  // the exact fades being suppressed. Double rAF: the first can fire before
  // the pending paint, the second is guaranteed to be a frame behind it.
  const [ssrNoTransitions, setSsrNoTransitions] = React.useState(deepLinkVisit);
  React.useEffect(() => {
    let raf = requestAnimationFrame(() => {
      raf = requestAnimationFrame(() => setSsrNoTransitions(false));
    });
    return () => cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
  }, []);

  // `handleOpenChange` needs the freshest active index when it writes the
  // opened URL: a trigger tap reports its index (onValueChange) before the
  // open commits, and state from the previous render would lag behind it.
  const indexRef = React.useRef(index);
  // Same discipline for `open` in `handleValueChange`: render-scope `open`
  // is the last COMMITTED value, so if a close and a value change ever landed
  // in the same task the guard below would see stale `true` and strand a
  // photo URL on a closed viewer. No current library path emits that ordering,
  // but the guard's correctness shouldn't depend on non-contractual event
  // ordering. (The library uses the same ref technique internally.)
  const openRef = React.useRef(open);

  // URL → lightbox. Covers the pathname changing underneath us — browser
  // back/forward — after the initial render (deep links already hydrate open,
  // so the mount run is a no-op). Gesture-driven changes wrote the URL
  // themselves in the callbacks below, so this no-ops for them too. URL-driven
  // flips render without the morph by design — Back closing the viewer fades,
  // it doesn't morph, matching how photo viewers behave elsewhere.
  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (urlIndex !== -1) {
      indexRef.current = urlIndex;
      openRef.current = true;
      setIndex(urlIndex);
      setOpen(true);
    } else {
      openRef.current = false;
      setOpen(false);
    }
  }, [urlIndex]);

  // The tab title follows the URL. Shallow History writes (below) never re-run
  // Next.js metadata — `generateMetadata` ran once, for the URL this page
  // LOADED with — so without this a deep-link visit keeps the first photo's
  // title forever: through every swipe and even after the viewer closes.
  // Owning the URL writes means owning the title too. Same strings as the
  // server metadata (shared helpers in photos.ts); the ` — ramka` suffix
  // mirrors the root layout's title template, which only applies server-side.
  // An effect (not the callbacks) so Back/Forward flips retitle as well.
  React.useEffect(() => {
    const base = open ? photoPageTitle(galleryPhotos[index]!) : GALLERY_PAGE_TITLE;
    document.title = `${base} — ramka`;
  }, [open, index]);

  // Lightbox → URL, written from the gesture callbacks — never from an effect,
  // so URL-driven prop flips can't echo back into history. The writes use the
  // native History API (Next.js shallow routing — `usePathname` stays in
  // sync); `router.push` would also work but round-trips the server on every
  // change, and shallow writes keep URL sync free even mid-swipe.
  const handleOpenChange = (nextOpen: boolean) => {
    openRef.current = nextOpen;
    setOpen(nextOpen);
    if (nextOpen) {
      // Opening pushes ONE history entry, so the browser Back button closes
      // the viewer instead of leaving the page.
      window.history.pushState(null, '', `${BASE_PATH}/${galleryPhotos[indexRef.current]!.id}`);
    } else {
      // Gesture closes REWRITE the entry instead of popping it. Never call
      // history.back() here: on a morph close this callback fires inside the
      // View Transition's DOM-update callback (state must commit between the
      // two snapshots), and a synchronous pop lands a popstate — router
      // re-render plus the popped entry's SCROLL RESTORATION — mid-morph.
      // When scrollTriggerIntoView had scrolled a half-visible tile into view
      // during the session, that restore yanks the page back between the VT
      // snapshots and the close visibly morphs onto the wrong tile. The cost
      // of replacing instead: one leftover grid history entry PER viewer
      // session (three sessions = four Backs to leave the page), and Back
      // onto an older grid entry replays that entry's scroll restoration —
      // if scrollTriggerIntoView moved the grid during the session, that
      // "no-op" Back visibly jumps the scroll position. Nothing breaks, and
      // the same jump would land mid-morph with history.back(); if a clean
      // stack matters more to you than morph closes, pop the entry from
      // onOpenChangeComplete(false) instead (after the transition settles).
      // `replaceState` is safe in the commit: it fires no popstate and
      // restores no scroll, and the async pathname re-render it triggers
      // reconciles to identical DOM.
      window.history.replaceState(null, '', BASE_PATH);
    }
  };

  const handleValueChange = (nextIndex: number) => {
    indexRef.current = nextIndex;
    setIndex(nextIndex);
    // Swiping / arrow keys REPLACE the current entry — no history spam.
    // Skipped while closed (via openRef, see above): a trigger tap reports its
    // index before the open commits, and handleOpenChange writes that URL.
    if (openRef.current) {
      window.history.replaceState(null, '', `${BASE_PATH}/${galleryPhotos[nextIndex]!.id}`);
    }
  };

  return (
    <ExampleShell
      title="URL-synced state"
      description="Every photo in this masonry wall is its own URL, driven by a Next.js dynamic route — the page lives at an [[...id]] optional catch-all, and the lightbox is controlled via open / value on Lightbox.Root. Tapping a tile opens the viewer and pushes /examples/lightbox/url-synced-state/5 with the native History API (shallow routing), swiping rewrites that URL in place, and the browser Back button closes the viewer. Loading a photo URL cold serves the viewer already open, straight from the server HTML with per-photo metadata: deep-link visits render the Portal in place (container={null}) instead of into document.body, which is what makes a server-rendered open lightbox possible at all — portals cannot be serialized into server HTML. Because the controlled props update synchronously from the gesture callbacks, trigger taps keep the view-transition morph."
      docsHref="/docs/lightbox/state-lifecycle"
      docsLabel="State & lifecycle docs"
    >
      <Lightbox.Root
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={handleOpenChange}
        value={index}
        onValueChange={handleValueChange}
        // Items register through effects, which never run on the server — so
        // without this an SSR-open page paints the counter as "6 of 0" until
        // hydration. `count` is the pre-registration fallback.
        count={galleryPhotos.length}
        loop
        scrollTriggerIntoView={[
          { type: 'onChange', behavior: 'instant' },
          { type: 'onOpenComplete', behavior: 'instant' },
        ]}
      >
        {/* Grid-span masonry — layout and rationale in masonry-grid.css, span
            math next to masonrySpan above. One DOM order for every viewport:
            the server HTML is correct at any width and the 2↔3 column switch
            is pure CSS, so refreshes never reshuffle. Each tile's own bottom
            gap is margin in the same row-units its span already counts;
            grid auto-placement drops each tile into the topmost open slot,
            which also keeps Tab order close to visual order (the old
            column-major bucketing zigzagged). */}
        <div className="lightbox-demo-masonry max-w-2xl">
          <div className="lightbox-demo-masonry-grid">
            {items.map((tile, tileIndex) => (
              <Lightbox.Trigger
                key={tile.id}
                index={tileIndex}
                className={`block w-full cursor-pointer overflow-hidden rounded-xl border-none bg-transparent p-0 ${triggerFocusClass}`}
                style={{
                  gridRowEnd: `span ${masonrySpan(tile.image)}`,
                  // The gap MUST be margin, not padding: the trigger is the
                  // view-transition morph target, and padding would grow its
                  // box past the visible image — the morph would land on a
                  // rect that includes the gap. Margin stays outside the
                  // border box (grid stretch subtracts it from the area), so
                  // the trigger's rect IS the image's rect.
                  marginBottom: `calc(var(--masonry-unit) * ${MASONRY_GAP_UNITS})`,
                }}
              >
                {({ imageRef }) => (
                  <Image
                    ref={imageRef}
                    src={tile.image}
                    alt={tile.alt}
                    placeholder="blur"
                    sizes="(min-width: 640px) 224px, 50vw"
                    loading="lazy"
                    className="block h-full w-full rounded-xl bg-neutral-100 object-cover transition duration-200 hover:opacity-90 dark:bg-neutral-800"
                  />
                )}
              </Lightbox.Trigger>
            ))}
          </div>
        </div>

        <LightboxGallery
          items={galleryItems}
          ariaLabel="Gallery photos"
          backdrop="solid"
          // Items register captions in effects, which never run on the server —
          // without this a deep-link visit paints an empty caption placard.
          // Fallback children render only until the registry fills, so it can't
          // go stale after a swipe.
          captionFallback={deepLinkVisit ? galleryPhotos[index]?.caption : undefined}
          // Server-rendered deep links paint the deep-linked slide, not slide 0
          // (library feature — forwarded to `Lightbox.Slides`). Inert for
          // regular visits: the stand-in only renders for server paint.
          ssrSlideShift
          portalProps={
            deepLinkVisit
              ? {
                  container: null,
                  className: `relative z-50${
                    ssrNoTransitions ? ' lightbox-demo-ssr-no-transitions' : ''
                  }`,
                }
              : undefined
          }
        />
      </Lightbox.Root>
    </ExampleShell>
  );
}
```

```ts examples/lightbox/url-synced-state/photos.ts
import type { StaticImageData } from 'next/image';

import { galleryImages } from './images.generated';

/**
 * Shared photo catalogue for the URL-synced state example. Plain data (no
 * `'use client'`) on purpose: the client demo maps it into grid tiles and
 * gallery slides, while the server route (`[[...id]]/page.tsx`) uses the same
 * ids and captions for `generateStaticParams`, per-photo metadata, and 404s —
 * one list, so a photo's URL can never drift from its slide.
 */
export interface GalleryPhoto {
  /**
   * URL segment for the photo's deep link (`…/url-synced-state/5`). An
   * opaque STABLE id — the routing looks photos up by this value, never by
   * array position, so reordering or removing photos can't repoint existing
   * links. (These happen to be numeric; any string works.)
   */
  id: string;
  alt: string;
  caption: string;
  image: StaticImageData;
}

/**
 * Page titles, shared by the server metadata (`[[...id]]/page.tsx`) and the
 * client demo. Shallow History API writes never re-run `generateMetadata` —
 * it ran once, for the URL the page LOADED with — so the demo mirrors the
 * title into `document.title` from the same state that drives the URL. One
 * source keeps the two from drifting. (The root layout's title template
 * appends the site suffix to these on the server.)
 */
export const GALLERY_PAGE_TITLE = 'URL-synced state example';

export function photoPageTitle(photo: GalleryPhoto): string {
  return `${photo.caption} — ${GALLERY_PAGE_TITLE}`;
}

export const galleryPhotos: GalleryPhoto[] = (
  [
    { id: '1', alt: 'Foggy pine ridge at dawn', caption: 'Dawn ridge' },
    { id: '2', alt: 'Empty coastal highway', caption: 'Open road' },
    { id: '3', alt: 'Overhead of a linen breakfast table', caption: 'Slow morning' },
    { id: '4', alt: 'Narrow sunlit alley', caption: 'Warm alley' },
    { id: '5', alt: 'Wide desert dunes', caption: 'Dunes' },
    { id: '6', alt: 'Rain on a window', caption: 'Rainy glass' },
    { id: '7', alt: 'Calm lake reflection', caption: 'Still water' },
    { id: '8', alt: 'Tall concrete staircase', caption: 'Ascent' },
    { id: '9', alt: 'Close-up of dried flowers', caption: 'Pressed petals' },
    { id: '10', alt: 'Panoramic city skyline at dusk', caption: 'Dusk skyline' },
    { id: '11', alt: 'Single tree in a green field', caption: 'Lone tree' },
    { id: '12', alt: 'Textured stone wall', caption: 'Stonework' },
  ] as const
).map((photo, i) => ({ ...photo, image: galleryImages[i]! }));
```

```css app/lightbox-demo/ssr-no-transitions.css
/*
 * No entrance motion when the page ITSELF is the entrance — used by
 * deep-linked visits that server-render the lightbox already open
 * (the URL-synced state example's dynamic route).
 *
 * The skin's open/close fades run off `@starting-style` (open-close.css,
 * chrome-hide, the strip's data-positioned reveal), and @starting-style
 * applies on an element's FIRST render — which, on a server-rendered open
 * viewer, is page load. A refreshed deep link would fade its own content in
 * as if it had just opened. While this class is on the Portal host every
 * transition inside is flattened, so the server paint IS the final frame.
 *
 * The demo removes the class one frame AFTER the first post-hydration paint
 * (not in the hydration commit): transitions consult the after-change style,
 * so dropping it in the same style recalc where e.g. the strip's
 * `data-positioned` lands would start the very fades being suppressed.
 *
 * (The companion problem — painting the RIGHT slide before hydration — is
 * library-owned: `Lightbox.Slides ssrSlideShift`, plus the skin mirroring the
 * track gap into `--lightbox-ssr-slide-gap` in lightbox-chrome.tsx. This file
 * is only about suppressing the skin's own fades.)
 */
.lightbox-demo-ssr-no-transitions *,
.lightbox-demo-ssr-no-transitions *::before,
.lightbox-demo-ssr-no-transitions *::after {
  transition: none !important;
}
```

```css app/lightbox-demo/thumbnail-strip-scroll-link.css
/**
 * Docs-only thumbnail-strip cosmetics (default gallery chrome).
 *
 * Library ThumbnailStrip owns midline padding, overflow clip, and the
 * ScrollTimeline → track transform link. Selection chrome here is a simple
 * floating square. Aspect-morph nine-slice lives on the debug recipes page.
 */

.lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip {
  --lightbox-demo-thumb-h: 4.5rem;
  --lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade: 40px;
  align-self: stretch;
  width: 100%;
  min-width: 0;
  /* Fits the floating indicator's overhang (3px gap + 2px stroke). */
  padding-block: 0.3125rem;
  /*
   * Soft clip on both edges. Stops at 25/50/75% of the fade use smoothstep
   * alphas (t²(3−2t)) so the dissolve eases in/out instead of a hard ramp.
   */
  -webkit-mask-image: linear-gradient(
    to right,
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0) 0,
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0.156) calc(var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade) * 0.25),
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5) calc(var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade) * 0.5),
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0.844) calc(var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade) * 0.75),
    #000 var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade),
    #000 calc(100% - var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade)),
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0.844) calc(100% - var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade) * 0.75),
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5) calc(100% - var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade) * 0.5),
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0.156) calc(100% - var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade) * 0.25),
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0) 100%
  );
  mask-image: linear-gradient(
    to right,
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0) 0,
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0.156) calc(var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade) * 0.25),
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5) calc(var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade) * 0.5),
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0.844) calc(var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade) * 0.75),
    #000 var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade),
    #000 calc(100% - var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade)),
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0.844) calc(100% - var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade) * 0.75),
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5) calc(100% - var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade) * 0.5),
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0.156) calc(100% - var(--lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-fade) * 0.25),
    rgb(0 0 0 / 0) 100%
  );
}

/*
 * Hidden until the library has positioned the track against the Slides
 * scroller (`data-positioned`, set in a layout effect before first client
 * paint). Client-side opens carry the attribute on their first painted frame,
 * so this never hides anything there. It only matters for pages that
 * server-render an open lightbox (URL-synced state deep links): scroll/transform
 * positions cannot be serialized into HTML, so the SSR'd strip sits at offset
 * 0 until hydration — a strip pointing at the wrong photo reads as broken,
 * a strip fading in a beat late reads as loading.
 */
.lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip:not([data-positioned]) {
  opacity: 0;
}

.lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip[data-positioned] {
  opacity: 1;
  transition: opacity 200ms ease-out;
}

.lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip [data-ramka-thumbnail-strip-track] {
  display: flex;
  width: max-content;
  gap: 0.625rem;
  align-items: center;
}

.lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip [role='tab'] {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  position: relative;
  display: block;
  width: var(--lightbox-demo-thumb-h);
  height: var(--lightbox-demo-thumb-h);
  flex-shrink: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  margin: 0;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 0.5rem;
  padding: 0;
  appearance: none;
  background: transparent;
}

.lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip [role='tab'] img {
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  object-fit: cover;
  pointer-events: none;
}

/* Stationary midline square — same size as a thumb + 3px gap + 2px stroke. */
.lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-indicator {
  position: absolute;
  left: 50%;
  top: 50%;
  box-sizing: border-box;
  width: calc(var(--lightbox-demo-thumb-h) + 10px);
  height: calc(var(--lightbox-demo-thumb-h) + 10px);
  border-radius: calc(0.5rem + 3px);
  border: 2px solid #000;
  pointer-events: none;
  transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
}

:is(.dark, [data-theme='dark']) .lightbox-demo-thumbnail-strip-indicator {
  border-color: #fff;
}

/* Thumb-jump slides crossfade CSS is injected by the library — tune with
   `--lightbox-select-vt-*` on Slides (or a parent). */
```

# Intercepted routes

The nextgram pattern: grid of plain Links, a @modal parallel-route slot, and an (.)photos/[id] intercepting route mounting an already-open controlled lightbox — Back closes it, hard loads get a standalone photo page (one URL, two presentations).

## Source

```tsx examples/lightbox/intercepted-routes/page.tsx
import type { Metadata } from 'next';
import Image from 'next/image';
import Link from 'next/link';

import { ExampleShell } from '../../../../_components/example-shell';
import { EXAMPLE_BASE_PATH, EXAMPLE_PAGE_TITLE, interceptedPhotos } from './photos';

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: EXAMPLE_PAGE_TITLE,
  description:
    'A photo grid wired to Next.js intercepted + parallel routes: clicking a tile soft-navigates to the photo URL and the lightbox opens in a @modal slot over the grid; loading that URL cold renders a standalone photo page instead. Built with ramka.',
};

/**
 * The grid is plain `<Link>`s — NOT `Lightbox.Trigger`s. Opening is a router
 * navigation: Next.js intercepts it (`@modal/(.)photos/[id]`) and mounts an
 * already-open lightbox in the layout's modal slot while this page stays on
 * screen underneath. That's the defining tradeoff of this pattern versus the
 * URL-synced state example: the open never flows through the library's
 * gesture path, so there is no trigger morph (the viewer fades in), and a
 * refresh on a photo URL renders a different presentation (the standalone
 * page) rather than this grid with the viewer open.
 *
 * `scroll={false}` keeps the grid's scroll position while the modal is up —
 * without it, Next scrolls the page to the top on every navigation.
 */
export default function InterceptedRoutesGridPage() {
  return (
    <ExampleShell
      title="Intercepted routes"
      description="The nextgram pattern: a grid of plain Next.js Links, a @modal parallel-route slot, and an (.)photos/[id] intercepting route that mounts an already-open, controlled lightbox during soft navigation — browser Back closes it. Hard-loading the same photo URL skips interception entirely and renders a standalone photo page: one URL, two presentations. Compare with the URL-synced state example, which keeps one presentation (grid + viewer) on refresh and keeps trigger morphs, at the cost of owning the History API writes itself."
      docsHref="/docs/lightbox/state-lifecycle"
      docsLabel="State & lifecycle docs"
    >
      <div className="grid max-w-2xl grid-cols-2 gap-4 sm:grid-cols-3">
        {interceptedPhotos.map((photo) => (
          <Link
            key={photo.id}
            href={`${EXAMPLE_BASE_PATH}/photos/${photo.id}`}
            scroll={false}
            className="block overflow-hidden rounded-xl"
          >
            <Image
              src={photo.image}
              alt={photo.alt}
              placeholder="blur"
              sizes="(min-width: 640px) 224px, 50vw"
              loading="lazy"
              className="block aspect-square h-auto w-full rounded-xl bg-neutral-100 object-cover transition duration-200 hover:opacity-90 dark:bg-neutral-800"
            />
          </Link>
        ))}
      </div>
    </ExampleShell>
  );
}
```

```tsx examples/lightbox/intercepted-routes/layout.tsx
/**
 * The layout is what makes the parallel-route slot exist: `@modal` renders as
 * the `modal` prop NEXT TO the page, not inside it. During soft navigation to
 * `photos/[id]` the interception route fills this slot with the lightbox while
 * `children` keeps showing the grid the user was on; on hard loads the slot
 * renders `@modal/default.tsx` (null) and `children` is the standalone photo
 * page.
 */
export default function InterceptedRoutesLayout({
  children,
  modal,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  modal: React.ReactNode;
}) {
  return (
    <>
      {children}
      {modal}
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx examples/lightbox/intercepted-routes/photo-modal.tsx
'use client';

import * as React from 'react';
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation';
import * as Lightbox from '@ramka/react/lightbox';

import { LightboxGallery } from '../../../../_components/lightbox-chrome';
import {
  EXAMPLE_BASE_PATH,
  EXAMPLE_PAGE_TITLE,
  interceptedPhotos,
  interceptedPhotoTitle,
} from './photos';

const items = interceptedPhotos.map((photo) => ({
  ...photo,
  src: photo.image,
  thumb: photo.image,
  // No `Lightbox.Trigger`s exist anywhere in this pattern (the grid is plain
  // Links), so no index has a trigger image and Ramka has nothing to bridge —
  // per the Next.js Image guide, the destination LQIP is the only loading
  // placeholder and belongs on every item.
  destinationBlur: true,
}));

/**
 * The viewer the intercepting route mounts: a self-contained, ALREADY-OPEN
 * controlled lightbox. There are no `Lightbox.Trigger`s here — the router
 * opened this, not a gesture, which is the pattern's defining tradeoff: the
 * open never flows through the library's gesture path, so it fades in rather
 * than morphing from the clicked tile.
 *
 * The default body portal is fine here (unlike the URL-synced state example's
 * `container={null}`): interception only happens during client-side
 * navigation, where `document.body` exists. Nothing about this component is
 * ever server-painted into the page.
 */
export function PhotoModal({ initialIndex }: { initialIndex: number }) {
  const router = useRouter();

  // Local `open` so a close gesture (Escape, ✕, pull-to-dismiss) can play the
  // skin's fade BEFORE the route unmounts this component: flipping the route
  // first (router.back() in onOpenChange) would yank the viewer out of the
  // DOM mid-frame. Browser Back does exactly that — popstate unmounts the
  // slot with no exit animation — which is unavoidable in this pattern.
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(true);
  const [index, setIndex] = React.useState(initialIndex);

  // Swipes REPLACE the current history entry with the new photo URL — no
  // history spam, and the grid entry underneath stays intact so one Back
  // always closes the viewer. replaceState is a shallow write: Next.js keeps
  // rendering this same mounted route (usePathname-style readers update, but
  // no navigation happens), so the viewer never remounts mid-swipe.
  const handleValueChange = (nextIndex: number) => {
    setIndex(nextIndex);
    window.history.replaceState(
      null,
      '',
      `${EXAMPLE_BASE_PATH}/photos/${interceptedPhotos[nextIndex]!.id}`,
    );
  };

  // Close = leave the photo route. router.back() (not push) pops the entry
  // the grid's <Link> pushed, so the history stack ends the session exactly
  // where it started. Deferred to onOpenChangeComplete so the fade finishes
  // first; the popstate then unmounts the @modal slot.
  const handleOpenChangeComplete = (isOpen: boolean) => {
    if (!isOpen) router.back();
  };

  // Shallow replaceState never re-runs route metadata, so swiping would
  // strand the tab title on the photo the modal opened with — same lesson as
  // the URL-synced state example: own the URL writes, own the title. The
  // ` — ramka` suffix mirrors the root layout's title template, which only
  // applies server-side.
  React.useEffect(() => {
    document.title = `${interceptedPhotoTitle(interceptedPhotos[index]!)} — ramka`;
  }, [index]);

  // Closing needs the same care: router.back() pops to the grid URL, but the
  // grid page in the `children` slot never changed, so Next.js has no
  // metadata update to apply — the photo title would stick to the grid.
  // Restore it when the slot unmounts (close and browser Back both land on
  // the grid, the only places this modal can exit to).
  React.useEffect(() => {
    return () => {
      document.title = `${EXAMPLE_PAGE_TITLE} — ramka`;
    };
  }, []);

  return (
    <Lightbox.Root
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={setOpen}
      onOpenChangeComplete={handleOpenChangeComplete}
      value={index}
      onValueChange={handleValueChange}
      // The Root mounts already open; `count` covers the render before the
      // items' registration effects run so the counter never reads "n of 0".
      count={interceptedPhotos.length}
      loop
    >
      <LightboxGallery
        items={items}
        ariaLabel="Gallery photos"
        backdrop="solid"
        // The Root mounts already open and captions register in effects (after
        // the first paint) — the fallback covers that first-paint window.
        captionFallback={interceptedPhotos[index]?.caption}
      />
    </Lightbox.Root>
  );
}
```

```ts examples/lightbox/intercepted-routes/photos.ts
import type { StaticImageData } from 'next/image';

// Static imports (not the download-images generator) — this example reuses the
// photo assets downloaded for the URL-synced state example, so there is no
// per-example image set to generate.
import p1 from '../../../../_assets/photos/mb-01.jpg';
import p2 from '../../../../_assets/photos/mb-02.jpg';
import p4 from '../../../../_assets/photos/mb-04.jpg';
import p5 from '../../../../_assets/photos/mb-05.jpg';
import p7 from '../../../../_assets/photos/mb-07.jpg';
import p8 from '../../../../_assets/photos/mb-08.jpg';
import p10 from '../../../../_assets/photos/mb-10.jpg';
import p11 from '../../../../_assets/photos/mb-11.jpg';

/**
 * Shared photo catalogue for the intercepted-routes example. One list serves
 * the grid page, the intercepted modal route, and the standalone photo page
 * (`photos/[id]/page.tsx`), so a photo's URL can never drift from its slide.
 */
export interface InterceptedPhoto {
  /**
   * URL segment for the photo route (`…/intercepted-routes/photos/5`). A
   * stable id looked up by value — never by array position — so reordering
   * or removing photos can't repoint existing links.
   */
  id: string;
  alt: string;
  caption: string;
  image: StaticImageData;
}

export const EXAMPLE_BASE_PATH = '/examples/lightbox/intercepted-routes';

export const EXAMPLE_PAGE_TITLE = 'Intercepted routes example';

export function interceptedPhotoTitle(photo: InterceptedPhoto): string {
  return `${photo.caption} — ${EXAMPLE_PAGE_TITLE}`;
}

export const interceptedPhotos: InterceptedPhoto[] = (
  [
    { id: '1', alt: 'Foggy pine ridge at dawn', caption: 'Dawn ridge' },
    { id: '2', alt: 'Empty coastal highway', caption: 'Open road' },
    { id: '3', alt: 'Narrow sunlit alley', caption: 'Warm alley' },
    { id: '4', alt: 'Wide desert dunes', caption: 'Dunes' },
    { id: '5', alt: 'Calm lake reflection', caption: 'Still water' },
    { id: '6', alt: 'Tall concrete staircase', caption: 'Ascent' },
    { id: '7', alt: 'Panoramic city skyline at dusk', caption: 'Dusk skyline' },
    { id: '8', alt: 'Single tree in a green field', caption: 'Lone tree' },
  ] as const
).map((photo, i) => ({ ...photo, image: [p1, p2, p4, p5, p7, p8, p10, p11][i]! }));
```

```tsx examples/lightbox/intercepted-routes/@modal/default.tsx
/**
 * Required for every parallel-route slot: rendered whenever the current URL
 * has no match inside `@modal` — the grid page, the standalone photo page on
 * a hard load, and any unmatched sibling route. Without it those URLs 404.
 */
export default function ModalDefault() {
  return null;
}
```

```tsx examples/lightbox/intercepted-routes/@modal/(.)photos/[id]/page.tsx
import { notFound } from 'next/navigation';

import { PhotoModal } from '../../../photo-modal';
import { interceptedPhotos } from '../../../photos';

/**
 * The intercepting route: `(.)` matches `photos/[id]` at the same segment
 * level, so a soft navigation from the grid renders THIS page into the
 * layout's `@modal` slot instead of navigating to the standalone photo page —
 * the grid stays mounted underneath. Hard loads never come here (interception
 * is client-navigation-only); they get `photos/[id]/page.tsx`.
 */
export default async function InterceptedPhotoRoute({
  params,
}: {
  params: Promise<{ id: string }>;
}) {
  const { id } = await params;
  const index = interceptedPhotos.findIndex((photo) => photo.id === id);
  if (index === -1) notFound();
  return <PhotoModal initialIndex={index} />;
}
```

```tsx examples/lightbox/intercepted-routes/photos/[id]/page.tsx
import type { Metadata } from 'next';
import Image from 'next/image';
import Link from 'next/link';
import { notFound } from 'next/navigation';

import {
  EXAMPLE_BASE_PATH,
  interceptedPhotos,
  interceptedPhotoTitle,
} from '../../photos';

/**
 * The hard-load presentation. Interception is a client-side navigation concept
 * only: a refresh, bookmark, or shared link of `…/photos/5` never touches
 * `@modal/(.)photos/[id]` — Next.js serves THIS standalone page instead
 * (Instagram's dedicated photo page is the same move). That is the pattern's
 * defining tradeoff: one URL, two presentations. If the refresh should keep
 * the grid + open-viewer presentation instead, that's the URL-synced state
 * example (dynamic route + container={null} + ssrSlideShift).
 */
interface PhotoPageProps {
  params: Promise<{ id: string }>;
}

export function generateStaticParams() {
  return interceptedPhotos.map((photo) => ({ id: photo.id }));
}

export async function generateMetadata({ params }: PhotoPageProps): Promise<Metadata> {
  const { id } = await params;
  const photo = interceptedPhotos.find((p) => p.id === id);
  if (!photo) return {};
  return {
    title: interceptedPhotoTitle(photo),
    description: `${photo.alt} — the standalone hard-load presentation of an intercepted photo route.`,
    openGraph: {
      title: interceptedPhotoTitle(photo),
      description: photo.alt,
      images: [
        {
          url: photo.image.src,
          width: photo.image.width,
          height: photo.image.height,
          alt: photo.alt,
        },
      ],
    },
    twitter: { card: 'summary_large_image' },
  };
}

export default async function StandalonePhotoPage({ params }: PhotoPageProps) {
  const { id } = await params;
  const photo = interceptedPhotos.find((p) => p.id === id);
  if (!photo) notFound();

  return (
    <div className="mx-auto w-full max-w-4xl px-6 py-14 md:px-10 md:py-16">
      <Link
        href={EXAMPLE_BASE_PATH}
        className="mb-8 inline-block text-[13px] text-neutral-500 underline underline-offset-4 hover:text-neutral-800 dark:hover:text-neutral-200"
      >
        ← Back to the gallery
      </Link>
      <figure>
        <Image
          src={photo.image}
          alt={photo.alt}
          placeholder="blur"
          sizes="(min-width: 896px) 832px, 100vw"
          priority
          className="block h-auto w-full rounded-2xl bg-neutral-100 dark:bg-neutral-800"
        />
        <figcaption className="mt-4 text-[15px] text-neutral-600 dark:text-neutral-300">
          {photo.caption}
        </figcaption>
      </figure>
      <p className="mt-8 max-w-2xl text-[13px] leading-6 text-neutral-500">
        You hard-loaded this photo URL, so route interception did not apply and you got this
        standalone page instead of the lightbox over the grid — one URL, two presentations. Navigate
        back to the gallery and click the same photo to see the intercepted modal presentation.
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

# Text message

iMessage-style chat with a single morphTo="origin" trigger over a stack of attachments.

## Source

```tsx examples/lightbox/text-message/page.tsx
'use client';

import Image from 'next/image';
import * as Lightbox from '@ramka/react/lightbox';

import { ExampleShell } from '../../../../_components/example-shell';
import {
  LightboxGallery,
  triggerFocusClass,
} from '../../../../_components/lightbox-chrome';
import { messageImageFiles } from './images.generated';

const messageImages = [
  {
    image: messageImageFiles[0]!,
    alt: 'Screenshot of a changelog notification',
  },
  {
    image: messageImageFiles[1]!,
    alt: 'Screenshot of a code review discussion',
    // Only the top of the stack registers an imageRef — the other attachments
    // rely on the destination Image's blur-up placeholder.
    destinationBlur: true,
  },
  {
    image: messageImageFiles[2]!,
    alt: 'Screenshot of a pull request overview',
    destinationBlur: true,
  },
].map((img) => ({ ...img, src: img.image, thumb: img.image }));

const stackRotations = [0, 2, -6];
const stackOffsets = [
  { x: 0, y: 0 },
  { x: 10, y: -4 },
  { x: -12, y: 8 },
];

export default function TextMessagePage() {
  return (
    <ExampleShell
      title="Text message"
      description={
        <>
          A single <code className="rounded bg-neutral-100 px-1 py-0.5 text-xs dark:bg-neutral-800">Lightbox.Trigger</code>{' '}
          wraps an entire stack of attachments. Paired with{' '}
          <code className="rounded bg-neutral-100 px-1 py-0.5 text-xs dark:bg-neutral-800">morphTo=&quot;origin&quot;</code>
          , the close animation always returns to the stack no matter which attachment is active.
        </>
      }
    >
      <div className="flex min-h-[80vh] items-end justify-end rounded-2xl bg-neutral-100 p-6 dark:bg-neutral-900">
        <Lightbox.Root morphTo="origin">
          <div className="flex max-w-[300px] flex-col items-end gap-3">
            <span className="text-[10px] font-medium uppercase tracking-[0.05em] text-neutral-500">
              Today at 11:11 AM
            </span>

            <div className="rounded-[20px] rounded-br-[4px] bg-blue-500 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-white">
              some imgs
            </div>

            <Lightbox.Trigger
              index={0}
              crossfade="close"
              className={`relative block h-80 w-[260px] cursor-pointer rounded-2xl border-none bg-transparent p-0 ${triggerFocusClass}`}
            >
              {({ morphRef, imageRef }) => (
                <div className="absolute -inset-5">
                  {messageImages.map((img, i) => {
                    const offset = stackOffsets[i] ?? { x: 0, y: 0 };
                    const rotation = stackRotations[i] ?? 0;
                    return (
                      <Image
                        key={img.alt}
                        src={img.image}
                        alt={img.alt}
                        placeholder="blur"
                        sizes="200px"
                        ref={
                          i === 0
                            ? (node) => {
                                morphRef(node);
                                imageRef(node);
                              }
                            : undefined
                        }
                        className="absolute block h-[280px] w-[200px] rounded-2xl object-cover shadow-[0_4px_20px_rgba(0,0,0,0.15)]"
                        style={{
                          left: '50%',
                          top: '50%',
                          transform: `translate(-50%, -50%) translate(${offset.x}px, ${offset.y}px) rotate(${rotation}deg)`,
                          zIndex: messageImages.length - i,
                        }}
                      />
                    );
                  })}
                </div>
              )}
            </Lightbox.Trigger>

            <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-xs text-neutral-500">
              <svg
                aria-hidden
                width="16"
                height="16"
                viewBox="0 0 16 16"
                fill="none"
                className="opacity-40"
              >
                <rect x="1" y="3" width="6" height="5" rx="1" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="1.2" />
                <rect x="5" y="1" width="6" height="5" rx="1" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="1.2" fill="currentColor" fillOpacity="0" />
                <rect x="9" y="3" width="6" height="5" rx="1" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="1.2" fill="currentColor" fillOpacity="0" />
                <rect x="3" y="8" width="10" height="7" rx="1.5" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="1.2" fill="currentColor" fillOpacity="0" />
              </svg>
              <span>{messageImages.length} attachments</span>
            </div>
          </div>

          <LightboxGallery items={messageImages} ariaLabel="Message attachments" />
        </Lightbox.Root>
      </div>
    </ExampleShell>
  );
}
```

# Film trailers

Movie posters morph into a fullscreen <video> that auto-plays on becoming active.

## Source

```tsx examples/lightbox/film-trailers/page.tsx
'use client';

import * as React from 'react';
import Image from 'next/image';
import * as Lightbox from '@ramka/react/lightbox';
import { Play } from 'lucide-react';

import { ExampleShell } from '../../../../_components/example-shell';
import {
  LightboxGallery,
  triggerFocusClass,
} from '../../../../_components/lightbox-chrome';
import { bbbPoster, edPoster, sintelPoster, tosPoster } from './images.generated';

/**
 * Blender Open Movies — real trailers/shorts with their official posters
 * (local copies of the Wikimedia Commons art, CC-BY Blender Foundation) so the
 * trigger thumbnail matches the video poster 1:1. Trailers are preferred where
 * available so the demo stays snappy to load.
 *
 * Each film is its own `Lightbox.Root` (no shared gallery) so opening one is a
 * single poster → fullscreen video morph.
 *
 * Media is sized to the *video* aspect (landscape), not the poster — so the
 * playing frame fills the fit-box without letterboxing. The open morph still
 * starts from the portrait poster (`crossfade="close"` hard-cuts into video).
 */
const films = [
  {
    id: 'bbb',
    title: 'Big Buck Bunny',
    year: 2008,
    genre: 'Animation',
    poster: bbbPoster,
    video: 'https://download.blender.org/peach/trailer/trailer_iphone.m4v',
    videoWidth: 480,
    videoHeight: 270,
  },
  {
    id: 'ed',
    title: "Elephant's Dream",
    year: 2006,
    genre: 'Sci-Fi',
    poster: edPoster,
    video: 'https://archive.org/download/ElephantsDream/ed_1024_512kb.mp4',
    videoWidth: 426,
    videoHeight: 240,
  },
  {
    id: 'sintel',
    title: 'Sintel',
    year: 2010,
    genre: 'Fantasy',
    poster: sintelPoster,
    video: 'https://download.blender.org/durian/trailer/sintel_trailer-720p.mp4',
    videoWidth: 1280,
    videoHeight: 720,
  },
  {
    id: 'tos',
    title: 'Tears of Steel',
    year: 2012,
    genre: 'Sci-Fi',
    poster: tosPoster,
    video: 'https://archive.org/download/Tears-of-Steel/tears_of_steel_720p.mp4',
    // Scope encode from the file (~2.39:1), not 16:9.
    videoWidth: 862,
    videoHeight: 360,
  },
];

function LightboxVideo({
  src,
  poster,
  readyToPlay,
  width,
  height,
}: {
  src: string;
  poster: string;
  /** True only after `onOpenChangeComplete(true)` — keeps playback off during the open morph. */
  readyToPlay: boolean;
  width: number;
  height: number;
}) {
  const videoRef = React.useRef<HTMLVideoElement>(null);

  // Autoplay only after the open transition finishes. While closed / mid-open /
  // closing, stay paused at 0 so the poster frame stays stable for the morph.
  React.useEffect(() => {
    const el = videoRef.current;
    if (!el) return;
    if (readyToPlay) {
      el.play().catch(() => {});
    } else {
      el.pause();
      el.currentTime = 0;
    }
  }, [readyToPlay]);

  return (
    <Lightbox.Zoom>
      {/* Media morphs + bridges the poster; video fills the sized host. */}
      <Lightbox.Media width={width} height={height} className="overflow-hidden rounded-xl">
        <video
          ref={videoRef}
          src={src}
          poster={poster}
          width={width}
          height={height}
          controls
          playsInline
          muted
          preload="metadata"
          className="object-cover"
        />
      </Lightbox.Media>
    </Lightbox.Zoom>
  );
}

function FilmLightbox({ film }: { film: (typeof films)[number] }) {
  const [readyToPlay, setReadyToPlay] = React.useState(false);

  return (
    <Lightbox.Root
      onOpenChange={(open) => {
        if (!open) setReadyToPlay(false);
      }}
      onOpenChangeComplete={(open) => {
        setReadyToPlay(open);
      }}
    >
      <Lightbox.Trigger
        index={0}
        // Hard-cut open (poster → video poster), dissolve on close (live frame → trigger).
        crossfade="close"
        className={`group block w-full cursor-pointer rounded-xl border-none bg-transparent p-0 text-left ${triggerFocusClass}`}
      >
        {({ morphRef }) => (
          <>
            {/* morphRef on the wrapper so poster + play affordance morph together. */}
            <div
              ref={morphRef}
              className={`relative overflow-hidden rounded-xl`}
            >
              <Image
                src={film.poster}
                alt={film.title}
                placeholder="blur"
                sizes="(min-width: 640px) 230px, 50vw"
                className="block aspect-[2/3] w-full rounded-xl object-cover"
                loading="lazy"
              />
              <div className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center rounded-xl bg-black/25 opacity-0 transition-opacity duration-200 group-hover:opacity-100">
                <div className="flex h-12 w-12 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-white/95 text-black">
                  <Play aria-hidden className="h-5 w-5 fill-current" />
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
            <div className="px-0.5 pt-2.5">
              <div className="text-sm font-medium leading-snug">{film.title}</div>
              <div className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
                {film.year} · {film.genre}
              </div>
            </div>
          </>
        )}
      </Lightbox.Trigger>

      <LightboxGallery
        items={[
          {
            id: film.id,
            src: film.poster,
            thumb: film.poster,
            alt: film.title,
            caption: film.title,
            width: film.videoWidth,
            height: film.videoHeight,
          },
        ]}
        ariaLabel={film.title}
        thumbnails="never"
        zoomControls={false}
        renderItem={() => (
          <LightboxVideo
            src={film.video}
            poster={film.poster.src}
            readyToPlay={readyToPlay}
            width={film.videoWidth}
            height={film.videoHeight}
          />
        )}
      />
    </Lightbox.Root>
  );
}

export default function FilmTrailersPage() {
  return (
    <ExampleShell
      title="Film trailers"
      description={
        <>
          Each poster is its own{' '}
          <code className="rounded bg-neutral-100 px-1 py-0.5 text-xs dark:bg-neutral-800">Lightbox.Root</code> with a
          single-item gallery and{' '}
          <code className="rounded bg-neutral-100 px-1 py-0.5 text-xs dark:bg-neutral-800">renderItem</code> for the
          video.{' '}
          <code className="rounded bg-neutral-100 px-1 py-0.5 text-xs dark:bg-neutral-800">crossfade=&quot;close&quot;</code>{' '}
          hard-cuts the open morph into the video and dissolves the live frame back into the poster on close. Video
          autoplays (muted) only after{' '}
          <code className="rounded bg-neutral-100 px-1 py-0.5 text-xs dark:bg-neutral-800">onOpenChangeComplete</code>.
        </>
      }
    >
      <div className="max-w-3xl">
        <div className="py-5">
          <div className="text-xs font-medium uppercase tracking-[0.08em] text-muted-foreground">
            Now Streaming
          </div>
          <h2 className="mt-1 text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight">Blender Open Movies</h2>
          <p className="mt-2 max-w-md text-sm text-muted-foreground">
            Four Creative Commons shorts from the Blender Foundation. Click any poster to watch fullscreen.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-5 sm:grid-cols-3">
          {films.map((film) => (
            <FilmLightbox key={film.id} film={film} />
          ))}
        </div>
      </div>
    </ExampleShell>
  );
}
```

# 3D models

Three.js product grid with Lightbox.Slides — onBeforeOpen preheats GLBs before the morph; shared orbit with each trigger.

## Source

```tsx examples/lightbox/3d-models/page.tsx
'use client';

import * as React from 'react';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { RoomEnvironment } from 'three/examples/jsm/environments/RoomEnvironment.js';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';
import { TrackballControls } from 'three/examples/jsm/controls/TrackballControls.js';
import * as Lightbox from '@ramka/react/lightbox';

import { ExampleShell } from '../../../../_components/example-shell';
import {
  LightboxGallery,
  triggerFocusClass,
} from '../../../../_components/lightbox-chrome';

const assetBase =
  'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/KhronosGroup/glTF-Sample-Assets@main/Models';

/** Shared square frame for every trigger + Media so tiles match in the grid. */
const FRAME_SIZE = 1024;

/** Each product mounts its own lightbox; trigger + Media each get a Three.js canvas. */
const products = [
  {
    id: 'shoe',
    name: 'Materials Variants Shoe',
    material: 'Leather · multi-variant',
    src: `${assetBase}/MaterialsVariantsShoe/glTF-Binary/MaterialsVariantsShoe.glb`,
  },
  {
    id: 'chair',
    name: 'Damask Chair',
    material: 'Purple & gold fabric',
    src: `${assetBase}/ChairDamaskPurplegold/glTF-Binary/ChairDamaskPurplegold.glb`,
  },
  {
    id: 'bottle',
    name: 'Water Bottle',
    material: 'Brushed metal',
    src: `${assetBase}/WaterBottle/glTF-Binary/WaterBottle.glb`,
  },
  {
    id: 'helmet',
    name: 'Damaged Helmet',
    material: 'Sci-fi prop',
    src: `${assetBase}/DamagedHelmet/glTF-Binary/DamagedHelmet.glb`,
  },
] as const;

type Product = (typeof products)[number];

const gltfCache = new Map<string, Promise<THREE.Group>>();

/** Underlying load promise (one scene per URL). Prefer {@link loadGltf} for mounts. */
function getGltfPromise(url: string): Promise<THREE.Group> {
  let hit = gltfCache.get(url);
  if (!hit) {
    hit = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      new GLTFLoader().load(
        url,
        (gltf) => resolve(gltf.scene),
        undefined,
        reject,
      );
    });
    gltfCache.set(url, hit);
  }
  return hit;
}

/** Clone a cached GLB for a canvas mount. */
function loadGltf(url: string): Promise<THREE.Group> {
  return getGltfPromise(url).then((scene) => scene.clone(true));
}

/**
 * Open-prepare gate: wait until the prepared lightbox canvas has loaded, synced
 * pose from the (still spinning) trigger, and painted — then start the VT.
 * We intentionally do NOT freeze spin: close feels smooth because motion stays
 * live through the morph; freezing until `onOpenChangeComplete` caused the
 * post-open “dead then start moving” hitch.
 */
type PaintGate = {
  painted: boolean;
  waiters: Set<() => void>;
};

const paintGates = new Map<string, PaintGate>();

function getPaintGate(productId: string): PaintGate {
  let gate = paintGates.get(productId);
  if (!gate) {
    gate = { painted: false, waiters: new Set() };
    paintGates.set(productId, gate);
  }
  return gate;
}

function resetPaintGate(productId: string) {
  const gate = getPaintGate(productId);
  gate.painted = false;
}

function markLightboxPainted(productId: string) {
  const gate = getPaintGate(productId);
  if (gate.painted) return;
  gate.painted = true;
  for (const waiter of gate.waiters) waiter();
  gate.waiters.clear();
}

/** Wait until the prepared lightbox has painted (or abort / timeout). Always resolves. */
function waitForLightboxPainted(
  productId: string,
  { signal, timeoutMs }: { signal: AbortSignal; timeoutMs: number },
): Promise<void> {
  const gate = getPaintGate(productId);
  if (signal.aborted || gate.painted) return Promise.resolve();

  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    let settled = false;
    const finish = () => {
      if (settled) return;
      settled = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      gate.waiters.delete(finish);
      signal.removeEventListener('abort', finish);
      resolve();
    };
    const timer = setTimeout(finish, timeoutMs);
    gate.waiters.add(finish);
    signal.addEventListener('abort', finish, { once: true });
    if (gate.painted) finish();
  });
}

/**
 * Center the model and scale so its longest axis is 1. Returns a wrapper at the
 * origin so every asset frames at the same camera distance.
 */
function normalizeModel(model: THREE.Object3D): THREE.Group {
  const wrapped = new THREE.Group();
  wrapped.add(model);
  model.updateWorldMatrix(true, true);

  const box = new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(model);
  const center = box.getCenter(new THREE.Vector3());
  const size = box.getSize(new THREE.Vector3());
  const maxDim = Math.max(size.x, size.y, size.z) || 1;

  model.position.sub(center);
  wrapped.scale.setScalar(1 / maxDim);
  wrapped.updateMatrixWorld(true);
  return wrapped;
}

/** Fixed framing for {@link normalizeModel} unit-sized roots (target at origin). */
function fitCameraToUnitObject(
  camera: THREE.PerspectiveCamera,
  controls: TrackballControls,
) {
  const maxSize = 1;
  const fitHeightDistance =
    maxSize / (2 * Math.tan(THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(camera.fov) / 2));
  const fitWidthDistance = fitHeightDistance / Math.max(camera.aspect, 0.001);
  const distance = 1.45 * Math.max(fitHeightDistance, fitWidthDistance);
  camera.near = distance / 100;
  camera.far = distance * 100;
  controls.target.set(0, 0, 0);
  camera.up.set(0, 1, 0);
  camera.position.set(distance * 0.35, distance * 0.2, distance);
  camera.lookAt(controls.target);
  camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
}

/**
 * Shared view orientation (no radius — each canvas keeps its own fit distance).
 * Trackball uses free camera.up, so we sync look-direction + up, not polar angles.
 * `spinAxis` / `spinSpeed` — one continuous coast that eases toward auto-spin.
 */
type ViewPose = {
  direction: [number, number, number];
  up: [number, number, number];
  spinAxis: [number, number, number];
  /** rad/s around {@link ViewPose.spinAxis} */
  spinSpeed: number;
};

type SpinState = {
  axis: THREE.Vector3;
  /** rad/s — eases toward {@link TARGET_SPIN_RAD_PER_SEC} after each flick */
  speed: number;
};

/** Trackball internals — used only to sample flick axis/speed on pointer up. */
type TrackballInertia = TrackballControls & {
  _eye: THREE.Vector3;
  _lastPosition: THREE.Vector3;
  _lastAxis: THREE.Vector3;
  _lastAngle: number;
};

type ViewStore = {
  pose: ViewPose | null;
  listeners: Set<(pose: ViewPose, source: symbol) => void>;
  set(pose: ViewPose, source: symbol): void;
  subscribe(fn: (pose: ViewPose, source: symbol) => void): () => void;
};

const viewStores = new Map<string, ViewStore>();

function getViewStore(productId: string): ViewStore {
  let store = viewStores.get(productId);
  if (!store) {
    store = {
      pose: null,
      listeners: new Set(),
      set(pose, source) {
        this.pose = pose;
        for (const listener of this.listeners) listener(pose, source);
      },
      subscribe(fn) {
        this.listeners.add(fn);
        return () => {
          this.listeners.delete(fn);
        };
      },
    };
    viewStores.set(productId, store);
  }
  return store;
}

const _offset = new THREE.Vector3();
const _direction = new THREE.Vector3();
const _up = new THREE.Vector3();

/** Auto-spin cruise speed — same units as OrbitControls.autoRotateSpeed (revs / 60s). */
const TRIGGER_AUTO_ROTATE_SPEED = 1;
const TARGET_SPIN_RAD_PER_SEC = ((2 * Math.PI) / 60) * TRIGGER_AUTO_ROTATE_SPEED;
/** How quickly flick speed eases into the cruise speed (higher = snappier). */
const SPIN_SPEED_BLEND = 2.2;

/** Unit look-direction + up; radius stays local to each canvas. */
function readViewPose(
  camera: THREE.PerspectiveCamera,
  controls: TrackballControls,
  spin: SpinState,
): ViewPose {
  _direction.copy(camera.position).sub(controls.target).normalize();
  _up.copy(camera.up).normalize();
  return {
    direction: [_direction.x, _direction.y, _direction.z],
    up: [_up.x, _up.y, _up.z],
    spinAxis: [spin.axis.x, spin.axis.y, spin.axis.z],
    spinSpeed: spin.speed,
  };
}

function applyViewPose(
  camera: THREE.PerspectiveCamera,
  controls: TrackballControls,
  pose: ViewPose,
  spin: SpinState,
) {
  const tb = controls as TrackballInertia;
  const radius = camera.position.distanceTo(controls.target) || 1;
  _direction.fromArray(pose.direction).normalize();
  _up.fromArray(pose.up).normalize();
  camera.position.copy(controls.target).addScaledVector(_direction, radius);
  camera.up.copy(_up);
  camera.lookAt(controls.target);
  tb._eye.subVectors(camera.position, controls.target);
  tb._lastPosition.copy(camera.position);
  // We own coasting — don't let Trackball damping fight the blended spin.
  tb._lastAngle = 0;
  if (pose.spinAxis[0] !== 0 || pose.spinAxis[1] !== 0 || pose.spinAxis[2] !== 0) {
    spin.axis.fromArray(pose.spinAxis).normalize();
  }
  if (Number.isFinite(pose.spinSpeed)) {
    spin.speed = Math.max(0, pose.spinSpeed);
  }
}

/** Sample flick axis + rad/s from Trackball, then clear its private damping. */
function captureFlickIntoSpin(
  controls: TrackballControls,
  spin: SpinState,
  dt: number,
) {
  const tb = controls as TrackballInertia;
  if (tb._lastAxis.lengthSq() > 1e-8) {
    spin.axis.copy(tb._lastAxis).normalize();
  }
  // `_lastAngle` is rad/frame; convert with the latest frame dt.
  const frameDt = Math.max(dt, 1 / 120);
  if (Math.abs(tb._lastAngle) > 1e-6) {
    spin.speed = Math.abs(tb._lastAngle) / frameDt;
  }
  tb._lastAngle = 0;
}

function applySpinStep(
  camera: THREE.PerspectiveCamera,
  controls: TrackballControls,
  spin: SpinState,
  dt: number,
) {
  // Ease flick velocity toward the cruise auto-spin — never drops through zero.
  const blend = 1 - Math.exp(-SPIN_SPEED_BLEND * dt);
  spin.speed += (TARGET_SPIN_RAD_PER_SEC - spin.speed) * blend;

  const angle = spin.speed * dt;
  if (Math.abs(angle) < 1e-8) return;

  _offset.copy(camera.position).sub(controls.target);
  _offset.applyAxisAngle(spin.axis, angle);
  camera.position.copy(controls.target).add(_offset);
  camera.up.applyAxisAngle(spin.axis, angle);
  camera.lookAt(controls.target);

  const tb = controls as TrackballInertia;
  tb._eye.subVectors(camera.position, controls.target);
  tb._lastPosition.copy(camera.position);
}

/**
 * Mount a disposable `<canvas>` inside `host` and bind Three.js to it.
 * Canvas is created/destroyed in the effect so `forceContextLoss` never
 * poisons a React-owned element (Strict Mode remount / reopen).
 * Free trackball rotate (no zoom/pan). Pose is synced across trigger + lightbox.
 */
function useThreeCanvas(
  hostRef: React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null>,
  product: Product,
  interactive: boolean,
  /** Idle spin for grid tiles; pause while lightbox is open so it doesn’t fight orbit. */
  autoRotate = false,
  /**
   * Lightbox canvases signal {@link markLightboxPainted} after a pose-synced
   * frame so `onBeforeOpen` can wait before the morph.
   */
  role: 'trigger' | 'lightbox' = 'trigger',
) {
  const controlsRef = React.useRef<TrackballControls | null>(null);
  const autoRotateRef = React.useRef(autoRotate);
  autoRotateRef.current = autoRotate;

  React.useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const host = hostRef.current;
    if (!host) return;

    // Own the canvas node — after forceContextLoss a canvas cannot host WebGL again.
    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    canvas.className = 'absolute inset-0 block size-full bg-transparent';
    canvas.style.touchAction = 'none';
    host.appendChild(canvas);

    const sourceId = Symbol(product.id);
    const store = getViewStore(product.id);
    let paintSignaled = false;
    if (role === 'lightbox') resetPaintGate(product.id);

    const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({
      canvas,
      antialias: true,
      alpha: true,
      premultipliedAlpha: false,
    });
    renderer.setClearColor(0x000000, 0);
    renderer.outputColorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
    renderer.toneMapping = THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping;
    renderer.toneMappingExposure = 1.15;

    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    const pmrem = new THREE.PMREMGenerator(renderer);
    const env = pmrem.fromScene(new RoomEnvironment(), 0.04).texture;
    scene.environment = env;
    pmrem.dispose();

    scene.add(new THREE.AmbientLight(0xffffff, 0.35));
    const key = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 1.6);
    key.position.set(2.5, 4, 3);
    scene.add(key);
    const fill = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 0.7);
    fill.position.set(-3, 1.5, -2);
    scene.add(fill);

    const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(40, 1, 0.1, 100);
    // Trackball (not Orbit): vertical drag can pass the poles without locking.
    const controls = new TrackballControls(camera, canvas);
    controls.noPan = true;
    controls.noZoom = true;
    controls.rotateSpeed = 1.4;
    controls.dynamicDampingFactor = 0.15;
    controls.enabled = interactive;
    controlsRef.current = controls;

    // Continuous spin state: flick speed eases into cruise auto-spin (no dead zone).
    const spin: SpinState = {
      axis: store.pose?.spinAxis
        ? new THREE.Vector3().fromArray(store.pose.spinAxis).normalize()
        : new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0),
      speed: store.pose?.spinSpeed ?? TARGET_SPIN_RAD_PER_SEC,
    };

    let frame = 0;
    let disposed = false;
    let applyingShared = false;
    let userDragging = false;
    let lastFrameTime = performance.now();
    let lastDt = 1 / 60;
    // Don't sync until the model is fitted — a pre-fit camera at the origin
    // would publish garbage poses into the store and twist the peer on open.
    let ready = false;

    const publishPose = () => {
      // Blocked while fitting / applying shared pose so a fresh lightbox fit
      // cannot clobber the trigger’s rotation in the store.
      if (!ready || applyingShared || disposed) return;
      store.set(readViewPose(camera, controls, spin), sourceId);
    };

    const onControlsChange = () => {
      publishPose();
    };
    controls.addEventListener('change', onControlsChange);

    // Pause idle spin while the user drags; on release, coast from flick → cruise.
    const onOrbitStart = () => {
      userDragging = true;
    };
    const onOrbitEnd = () => {
      userDragging = false;
      captureFlickIntoSpin(controls, spin, lastDt);
      publishPose();
    };
    controls.addEventListener('start', onOrbitStart);
    controls.addEventListener('end', onOrbitEnd);

    const unsub = store.subscribe((pose, source) => {
      if (!ready || source === sourceId || disposed) return;
      applyingShared = true;
      applyViewPose(camera, controls, pose, spin);
      applyingShared = false;
    });

    const setSize = () => {
      const width = host.clientWidth;
      const height = host.clientHeight;
      if (width < 1 || height < 1) return;
      const dpr = Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2);
      renderer.setPixelRatio(dpr);
      renderer.setSize(width, height, false);
      camera.aspect = width / height;
      camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
      controls.handleResize();
    };

    const signalPaintedIfNeeded = () => {
      if (role !== 'lightbox' || !ready || disposed || paintSignaled) return;
      if (host.clientWidth < 1 || host.clientHeight < 1) return;

      paintSignaled = true;
      // Sync to the live trigger pose, then paint before the VT captures "new".
      if (store.pose) {
        applyingShared = true;
        applyViewPose(camera, controls, store.pose, spin);
        applyingShared = false;
      }
      setSize();
      controls.update();
      renderer.render(scene, camera);
      // Two rAFs: one for the GL submit, one so the composited canvas is current.
      requestAnimationFrame(() => {
        if (disposed) return;
        requestAnimationFrame(() => {
          if (disposed) return;
          markLightboxPainted(product.id);
        });
      });
    };

    const render = () => {
      if (disposed) return;
      const now = performance.now();
      const dt = Math.min((now - lastFrameTime) / 1000, 0.1);
      lastFrameTime = now;
      lastDt = dt;
```
